_README: Classified divergences for ci/fixture_ab.sh - both engines against RVF's own
regression fixture, per assertion, in about 45 seconds.
Its own file because the fixture is not a release. A cause proven on 58 files
of deliberately broken 2013 test data transfers nowhere else. This arm also
loads ci/known-engine-divergences.json, whose entries are engine defects
rather than release facts, and which therefore do apply here.
STATE 2026-09-10, all three SQL groups: 210 assertions joined, 209 identical
(99.5%), 1 divergent - the entry below. MySQL 159 failures, DuckDB 158.
THE FIVE RAGGED-ROW ENTRIES ARE GONE, and how they went is the point of this
arm. They were 20 malformed rows across both fixtures: a TAB inside three
terms (splitting one field into two), sixteen rows missing caseSignificanceId
entirely, and one association row with a double tab leaving an empty field.
The tab sat at a DIFFERENT position in Delta than in Snapshot for the same
description id, which is what proved it was corruption and not a designed
case - no test case differs per file. Repairing them took this arm from 5
divergences to 0 on release-type-validation, and moved seven DuckDB
assertions' findings DOWN to MySQL's numbers: DuckDB had been reporting
findings about the corruption itself.
WHY THE PACKAGE IS REPACKED AS CRLF: RF2 files are CRLF and RVF's MySQL
loader says so - `lines terminated by '\r\n' ignore 1 lines`. The fixture is
LF-only, so that statement read each file as ONE line, discarded it, and
loaded 0 rows with no error: 90 empty tables and every previous-dependent
assertion passing over nothing. Before that normalisation this arm read 50.9%
identical and every MySQL number in it was meaningless.
RETIRED 2026-09-10: 2e0eb135 / duckdb-does-not-pad-trailing-spaces-in-string-comparison.
DuckBinder now reproduces MySQL's PAD SPACE comparison where it can - a
statement that GROUPS BY term, and is not grouping inside a derived table, has
its term references wrapped in rtrim(). Both engines now report 169 failures
on this fixture and 212 of 213 assertions agree.
It is NOT reproduced for term JOINS, and that is a decision rather than an
omission: rewriting those made three assertions fail to execute at all -
unique-FSN, unique-fsn-case-insensitive-checking and unique-preferred-terms
each group by term INSIDE a derived table and then join the outer query on
dup.term, so rewriting the inner projection renames the column and the outer
reference stops resolving. Three assertions that do not run is a worse report
than one false negative. 21 statements in 19 assertions carry that exposure,
none of them divergent on any release measured so far, and doing it properly
needs the parse tree - in the publisher that transpiles the corpus, not here.

_README: Assertions one engine reports that the other does not. Zero here, and it
